orbital_description: The book opens the science of food chains through the specific energy transfer from producers to consumers to decomposers, the habitats of each linked creature, and the concept that food chains are more accurately food webs. Neal's geometric illustrations make the connections visual before the text names them.

title: Dawn: Watch the World Awaken
author: Marc Martin
orbital_description: The 2026 ALSC Notable Book opens nature observation through the specific sequence of dawn: which animals stir first and why, the physics of light changing the landscape, the ecology of a forest lake at sunrise. Martin's art makes the moment feel like witnessing something private and true.

title: Debbie Allen's Rise to Fame
author: Tami Charles
orbital_description: Fall 2025 pub. Tami Charles opens the history of racial segregation in arts education through Debbie Allen's specific experience being rejected from the Houston Foundation for Ballet because of her race, the subsequent path through Broadway and Hollywood to Fame and Grey's Anatomy, and the concept of creative work as a form of sustained resistance.

title: Diary of a Spider
author: Doreen Cronin
orbital_description: The book introduces arachnid biology including webs, molting, and silk production through the same comic diary format as its companion, while exploring cross-species relationships and the experience of being feared.

title: Don't Let the Pigeon Drive the Bus
author: Mo Willems
orbital_description: The book breaks the fourth wall to make children active participants; the pigeon's escalating negotiation tactics introduce persuasion, argumentation, and the art of saying no. Every tactic the pigeon uses is a real rhetorical strategy.

title: Don't Trust Fish
author: Neil Sharpson
orbital_description: NPR named this one of the funniest picture books of 2025. Sharpson's conspiracy-theory premise and Santat's cinematic illustrations build a joke that pays off on every spread. Beneath the absurdity is a genuine lesson in unreliable narration and the difference between assertion and evidence.

title: Dragon Flower
author: Chen Jiang Hong
orbital_description: The NYT Best Illustrated 2025 winner opens Chinese mythology through the dragon as a water and weather deity, the history of Chinese ink brush painting as a traditional art form, the geography of classical Chinese landscapes, and the ecological concept of interdependence. Translated from the French by Alyson Waters.

title: Dragons Love Tacos
author: Adam Rubin
orbital_description: The book is pure delight engineering: the cause-and-effect logic of spicy salsa causing dragon fire is genuinely funny and genuinely logical. It rewards careful attention and predicting what happens next.

title: Duck and Goose
author: Tad Hills
orbital_description: The book models conflict over a shared resource, the humiliation of being wrong, and the repair of a friendship built on a mistake. The polka-dotted ball is a gentle lesson in assumptions.

title: El Deafo
author: Cece Bell
orbital_description: Newbery Honor 2015. Opens the biology of hearing including how the cochlea processes sound and what meningitis damages, the history of hearing aid technology through the specific Phonic Ear Bell wears, and the social-emotional experience of disability and identity through the graphic memoir form's ability to show interior experience.

title: Elf Dog and Owl Head
author: M.T. Anderson
orbital_description: The 2024 Newbery Honor novel opens suburban ecology and geography through a magical realist lens, the philosophy of transformation, and the specific anxiety of not knowing whether the strange thing you love is safe. Anderson's dark comic sensibility and Wu's ethereal illustrations create something genuinely uncategorizable.

title: Escape from Mr. Lemoncello's Library
author: Chris Grabenstein
orbital_description: Opens the history of libraries through a puzzle-game built around literary knowledge, information literacy (finding what you need in a vast collection), the Dewey Decimal System as an actual navigational tool, and the dynamics of collaboration vs. competition under pressure. The puzzles are real and solvable.

title: Everywhere, Wonder
author: Matthew Swanson
orbital_description: Matthew Swanson and Robbi Behr built this book around questions, not answers. Why do leaves change color? Where does the wind start? The illustrations move through biomes and seasons, carrying ecology, meteorology, and botany in the background while the text models scientific curiosity as a daily practice. The child finishes this book wanting to go outside and look at something closely, which is the entire point.

title: Fablehaven
author: Brandon Mull
orbital_description: The book is built on ecological logic: the preserve is a managed habitat for creatures that would destroy each other and humans without governance. The creatures follow internally consistent rules. Connecticut geography anchors the fantasy.

title: Fia Hosein Finds Her Beat
author: Tracey Baptiste
orbital_description: Lit Hub Most Anticipated 2026, praised by Kate Messner. Tracey Baptiste (The Jumbies, African Icons) opens the linguistics of accent and language shift in immigrant children, the geography and culture of Trinidad, and the specific social-emotional experience of assimilation as loss rather than gain. Part of The Kids in Mrs. Z's Class series — readable in any order.

title: Fireworks
author: Matthew Burgess
orbital_description: The 2026 Caldecott Medal winner opens light physics through the fireworks display, urban geography through a city neighborhood in summer heat, and the science of anticipation. Chien's vertical gatefold pages open like a real explosion of color.

title: Found Sound
author: Meg Wolitzer and Charlie Panek
orbital_description: PW Spring 2026 preview. Co-written by Meg Wolitzer (one of America's most acclaimed adult novelists, making her children's debut) and her son. Opens acoustics and the physics of sound through the scavenger hunt structure, the concept of found sound as a musical tradition, and the community history embedded in music.

title: Frizzy
author: Claribel A. Ortega
orbital_description: The 2023 Belpré Award winner opens Dominican-American cultural identity, the history of European beauty standards imposed on Black and Latina women, family intergenerational patterns, and the social economics of hair in a community where straightening is a ritual. The graphic novel format makes the visual transformation deeply felt.

title: From Seed to Plant
author: Gail Gibbons
orbital_description: The book covers pollination with named insect pollinators, seed dispersal mechanisms, germination, and plant anatomy with labeled diagrams. It is the foundation for every plant science conversation for years to come.

title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler
author: E.L. Konigsburg
orbital_description: Newbery Medal 1968. Opens the collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, art historical methods for authenticating Renaissance works, New York City geography, and the concept of living invisibly inside a public institution. The survival logistics make it an engineering puzzle.

title: Good Golden Sun
author: Brendan Wenzel
orbital_description: SLJ Best Picture Book 2025. Brendan Wenzel (Hello, I'm Here!; They All Saw a Cat, Caldecott Honor) opens solar energy as the foundation of all ecosystems through the visual language of energy flow — from sun to plant to insect to bird to decomposer — in a circular narrative that models photosynthesis and the food web.

title: Goodnight Gorilla
author: Peggy Rathmann
orbital_description: The wordless-adjacent format requires children to narrate from visual cues, building storytelling and sequencing skills. The parade of animals introduces zoo species; the zookeeper's wife's discovery is a perfect setup-and-reveal.

title: Grumpy Monkey
author: Suzanne Lang
orbital_description: The book validates the full range of emotions including the right to feel bad without explanation. Grumpy Monkey pushes back against forced positivity with humor, modeling emotional self-awareness and the value of simply sitting with a feeling.

title: Hair Love
author: Matthew A. Cherry
orbital_description: Texture science, problem-solving, Black hair culture, and fatherhood as practice. Academy Award-winning short film origin.
heads_up: The reason Mom is absent is revealed at the end.

title: Hattie Mae Begins Again
author: Sharon G. Flake
orbital_description: Pub January 13, 2026. Sharon Flake (The Skin I'm In, Coretta Scott King Author Award) opens the historical geography of the Great Migration and Black boarding school culture in 1930s America, the class dynamics within Black communities during the Depression, and the social-emotional architecture of belonging in a space where every signal says you don't fit.

title: Hello, Stranger
author: Barbara O'Connor
orbital_description: The book opens rural North Carolina geography and the social texture of small-town life, the biology of stray dog behavior, and the mechanics of friendship between two people who don't know how to start one. O'Connor's regional setting is rendered with the specificity of someone who knows the landscape intimately.

title: Honeybird Blue
author: Taunya English
orbital_description: PW Spring 2026 Sneak Preview. Opens the ornithology of bird coloration including the biology of feather pigmentation and structural color, the ecology of local bird habitats, and the social-emotional architecture of a parent-child nature walk as a form of intergenerational attention.

title: How a Bear Became a Book: The Collaboration That Created Winnie-the-Pooh
author: Annette Bay Pimentel
orbital_description: Multiple starred reviews from MacKids 2026 roundup. Opens the natural history of bears, the WWI history behind A.A. Milne's military service and the bear named after Winnipeg, the craft of picture book collaboration between writer and illustrator, and the history of British children's literature in the early 20th century. From the author of Before Colors.

title: How a House Is Built
author: Gail Gibbons
orbital_description: The book tracks a full construction sequence: surveying, foundation, framing, roofing, plumbing, electrical, and finishing. Each trade is named and visualized. Children who read this look at every building they enter differently.

title: How Dinosaurs Went Extinct: A Safety Guide
author: Ame Dyckman
orbital_description: The book opens paleontology and mass extinction science through a comedy premise: each dinosaur species died because it ignored a specific safety guideline. Children absorb real extinction causes including the Chicxulub asteroid, climate change, and food chain collapse while laughing at absurd safety posters.

title: How Do Dinosaurs Say Goodnight
author: Jane Yolen
orbital_description: Every dinosaur is real and named: Stegosaurus, Ankylosaurus, Tyrannosaurus Rex. The bad bedtime behavior maps to real child behavior; the eventual compliance is reassuring. Children absorb dinosaur taxonomy through a bedtime routine.

title: How to Find a Fox
author: Nilah Magruder
orbital_description: Nilah Magruder sends a Black girl into the forest with a field guide, a backpack, and a plan. The fox never appears. What appears instead is the entire woodland ecosystem: tracks, scat, burrows, birdsong, lichen, mushrooms. The child absorbs tracking skills, woodland ecology, and the scientific principle that failed experiments still produce data. The girl is not disappointed. She is loaded with evidence. She will come back tomorrow.

title: How to Hatch: A Gosling's Guide to Breaking Free
author: Sara Holly Ackerman
orbital_description: PW starred. Opens egg biology including air cell development, the pip reflex, and the mechanics of breaking through a shell, presented as a first-person narration that simultaneously describes the science and models persistence under difficulty. The dual function is remarkably clean.

title: How to Write a Poem
author: Kwame Alexander
orbital_description: The book opens the craft of poetry through the instruction itself becoming the poem: each page demonstrates the technique it describes. Sweet's mixed-media collage illustrations model the same aesthetic principle — found materials assembled into something beautiful. Children who read this write differently.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
author: Diana Wynne Jones
orbital_description: Opens the fairy tale tradition through radical subversion of the eldest-daughter-must-fail narrative, the geography and folklore of a fantasy Wales, the philosophy of identity through a protagonist who discovers herself by being forced to be old, and Diana Wynne Jones's signature misdirection comedy. The Miyazaki film is good; the book is richer.

title: I Will Always Write Back: How One Letter Changed Two Lives
author: Caitlin Alifirenka and Martin Ganda with Liz Welch
orbital_description: Opens the geography and economic history of Zimbabwe through Martin's descriptions of daily life under hyperinflation and poverty, the history of the pen pal tradition as an educational practice, and the social-emotional concept of correspondence as a form of intimacy that crosses radical inequality.

title: If You Give a Pig a Pancake
author: Laura Numeroff
orbital_description: This companion book extends the cause-and-effect model while introducing where maple syrup comes from, cooking chemistry, and the natural source of pancake ingredients. The sequence layers math onto food systems.

title: If You Plant a Seed
author: Kadir Nelson
orbital_description: Nearly wordless. Plant growth cycles, soil and water requirements, and social concepts of generosity.

title: In a Small Small Pond
author: Denise Fleming
orbital_description: Every creature named is real: heron, tadpole, dragonfly, turtle. The seasonal arc from spring to winter maps a full ecological cycle. The rhyming couplets make the vocabulary stick in ways prose cannot.

title: In the Desert
author: David Elliott
orbital_description: Confirmed March 18, 2025. David Elliott and Gordy Wright open Saharan desert ecology through the specific organisms that survive in one of Earth's most extreme environments, the geography of the Sahara as an ecosystem rather than an absence, and the literary technique of a poem as a concentrated lens on natural observation.

title: In the Desert: Poems of the Sahara
author: David Elliott
orbital_description: Confirmed March 18, 2025. This standalone listing provides the correct title. Opens Saharan ecology through the lives of animals that survive in one of Earth's most extreme environments — the fennec fox's ears, the sidewinder's diagonal track, the date palm's root system — each rendered in a poem that doubles as biological observation.
heads_up: NOTE: This duplicates entry #17 (In the Desert) in this batch. Claude Code should deduplicate before import.

title: Inkheart
author: Cornelia Funke
orbital_description: Opens the craft of reading aloud and oral storytelling traditions, the geography of northern Italy through the family's hiding places, the concept of fiction as a world with internal logical rules that continue when characters leave it, and the literary history of the book-within-a-book structure.

title: Invisible Things
author: Andy J. Pizza
orbital_description: The book opens physics through invisible forces including gravity and magnetism and sound waves, biology through the invisible processes of growth and digestion, and philosophy through the invisible qualities of friendship and love. Pizza's visual design makes abstract science tangible.

title: Ish
author: Peter Reynolds
orbital_description: The book dismantles perfectionism by naming the alternative: ish. A vase-ish picture. A tree-ish picture. The concept gives children permission to make art that isn't finished or correct, which is where all real creative work begins.

title: Island Storm
author: Brian Floca
orbital_description: The Kirkus Prize Finalist opens meteorology through a coastal storm system including atmospheric pressure changes visible as darkening sky and wind shifts, the geography of a small seaside town, and the developmental psychology of exploring boundaries. Floca (Locomotive, Caldecott Medal) and Smith (Sidewalk Flowers, Caldecott Honor) together are at the top of their field.

title: J vs. K
author: Jerry Craft and Kwame Alexander
orbital_description: The book opens the creative process of both writing and illustration through a story about students discovering their creative identities. The hybrid format models both prose writing and sequential art, making the craft visible while also delivering a genuine story about competition and collaboration.

title: Knuffle Bunny
author: Mo Willems
orbital_description: The book captures the exact experience of pre-verbal communication and the desperation of not being understood. The Brooklyn neighborhood photographs anchor the story in real geography; the dialogue between father and toddler is phonologically precise.

title: Legendary Frybread Drive-In: Intertribal Stories
author: edited by Cynthia Leitich Smith
orbital_description: The Printz Award winner opens the geography and political history of Native American tribal sovereignty, the concept of intertribal as distinct from a single indigenous identity, the diverse literary voices of Native American authors writing across genre, and the social-emotional experience of Native teenagers navigating two worlds. The title comes from a real place that is a community gathering point.

title: Lilly's Purple Plastic Purse
author: Kevin Henkes
orbital_description: The book moves through impulse, action, consequence, regret, repair, and forgiveness in ten pages, mapping the full arc of a relational rupture and reconciliation. Writing the note makes literacy feel emotionally consequential.

title: Little Blue Truck
author: Alice Schertle
orbital_description: The book models the social return on investment of kindness: Blue's habit of greeting animals pays dividends when he needs help. Farm animal names and sounds are a bonus biology lesson.

title: Little Rebels
author: Yuyi Morales
orbital_description: The NYT Best Illustrated 2025 winner and Caldecott and Pura Belpré Honor author's latest opens the history of child and youth activism across cultures and centuries, the concept of civil resistance as a historical constant, and the social-emotional idea that children have been agents of change in their own right across history.

title: Lola
author: Karla Arenas Valenti
orbital_description: The 2025 Belpré Award winner weaves Mexican folk tradition into a modern fable about desire, consequence, and the meaning of knowing yourself. The dueling spirit structure maps a genuine choice architecture that children experience daily in smaller form.

title: Mae and Gerty and the Matter with Matter
author: Elaine Vickers
orbital_description: The book opens the three states of matter through the relationship between two opposite sisters: one orderly and solid, one scattered and gaseous. The metaphor is scientifically accurate and emotionally precise. Children absorb the properties of solids, liquids, and gases through a sibling story they recognize.

title: Maizy Chen's Last Chance
author: Lisa Yee
orbital_description: The 2023 Newbery Honor book opens Chinese American immigration history through the specific lens of a family restaurant, small-town California geography, and the secrets families keep across generations. Every clue Maizy finds is a lesson in American history she was never taught in school.

title: Mama Panya's Pancakes
author: Mary Chamberlin & Rich Chamberlin
orbital_description: Mary and Rich Chamberlin set this in a Kenyan village where Adamu invites everyone he passes on the way to market for Mama Panya's pancakes. Swahili words are woven into the text. Julia Cairns' illustrations carry East African market culture, agricultural products, and village architecture. The child absorbs Swahili vocabulary, Kenyan daily life, counting and addition (how many guests now?), the economics of communal sharing, and the resolution: every guest brings something, and two pancakes become a feast. The math problem is real. The solution is social.

title: Maniac Magee
author: Jerry Spinelli
orbital_description: Newbery Medal 1991. Opens the history of de facto racial segregation in Northern cities through the geography of Two Mills, Pennsylvania, the physics of long-distance running through Maniac's abilities, and the concept of a folk legend as a narrative device that elevates ordinary social reality to mythological scale.

title: Maybe Something Beautiful
author: F. Isabel Campoy & Theresa Howell
orbital_description: Based on the real Urban Art Trail in San Diego's Barrio Logan, this book follows Mira as she meets a muralist and helps transform her gray neighborhood into an outdoor gallery. Rafael Lopez (who actually painted those real murals) illustrates the transformation with his signature saturated style. The child absorbs public art as civic participation, color theory, community organizing, and the idea that beauty is not a luxury but infrastructure. The gray-to-color visual arc teaches without narrating.

title: Mixed: A Colorful Story
author: Arree Chung
orbital_description: Arree Chung personifies primary colors as communities that segregate by hue. Reds shout. Blues are cool. Yellows shine. They separate. Then a Red and a Yellow have an Orange child, and the boundaries dissolve. The child absorbs color theory (primary, secondary, tertiary mixing), the social mechanics of segregation and integration, and the art-science intersection of pigment behavior. The allegory works for toddlers as a color lesson and for older children as a community story. The science is real. The metaphor is earned.

title: Moon Song
author: Michaela Goade
orbital_description: SLJ Best Picture Book 2025. Caldecott Honor illustrator Michaela Goade (Berry Song) opens Tlingit and Haida cosmology through the moon as a living presence in the forest and ocean, Pacific Northwest ecology and geography, and the concept of traditional cultural knowledge as a distinct way of understanding the natural world.

title: My Heart Fills with Happiness
author: Monique Gray Smith
orbital_description: Sensory experience as emotional vocabulary. Cree and Metis visual culture. Board book.

title: My Presentation Today Is About the Anaconda
author: Bibi Dumon Tak
orbital_description: Kirkus Spring 2025 Preview praised as 'raises the bar for animal nonfiction.' Translated from Dutch. Every animal's oral report is delivered from its ecological relationship to the subject, making the science accurate and the humor arise from perspective. The format teaches predator-prey relationships, habitat ecology, and the scientific names of real species.

title: Napesni/Renegade: The Story of a Wild Bison
author: Marcie R. Rendon
orbital_description: Fall 2025. Marcie R. Rendon (Cash and the Bears, multiple award-winning Ojibwe author) opens the history of American bison from 30 million animals to near extinction in the 1880s through the specific story of one wild bison's capture and relocation, the ecology of bison as keystone species in prairie ecosystems, and the indigenous land rights context of bison management on reservations.

title: Nell Plants a Tree
author: Anne Wynter
orbital_description: The book opens forest ecology through a tree's life cycle, community history through the generations of people who grow up near the same tree, and the philosophy of planting something you won't live to see fully grown. Miyares's illustrations render the passage of time through changing light and season.

title: Not a Box
author: Antoinette Portis
orbital_description: The simplest lesson in creative thinking. The foundational cognitive move behind engineering, art, and science.

title: Octopus Moon
author: Bobbie Pyron
orbital_description: 2026 Schneider Family Book Award Honor (middle grade). Opens octopus neurobiology including distributed intelligence across eight arms, camouflage and color-change mechanisms, and the cognitive science of octopus problem-solving, alongside the social-emotional experience of a child who finds connection through an animal that also lives in its own particular way. NOTE: Likely pub 2025 — verify before placing on 2026 shelf.

title: Omnivore's Dilemma: Young Readers Edition
author: Michael Pollan
orbital_description: Adapted from Pollan's landmark adult work for young readers. Opens the ecology and economics of the American industrial food system through corn as its foundational crop, the concept of a food chain as a linked system from soil to stomach, the chemistry of photosynthesis as the origin of all food calories, and the comparison of industrial vs. local vs. hunter-gatherer food systems.

title: One Day a Mayfly
author: Shirley Marr
orbital_description: Confirmed May 27, 2025. Opens the entomology of Ephemeroptera (mayflies) including the extraordinary biology of an insect that lives its adult life in a single day after spending up to two years as a nymph, the urban freshwater ecology of a city lake, and the philosophical concept of a life measured in quality rather than duration.
heads_up: The mayfly lives and dies within a single day; mortality is central.

title: One Day at the Bottom of the Deep Blue Sea
author: Daniel Bernstrom
orbital_description: Confirmed April 29, 2025. Daniel Bernstrom (One Day in the Eucalyptus, Eucalyptus Tree) opens deep-sea biology through the adventure structure of a girl navigating the ocean's darkest layers, the ecology of deep-sea predators, and the specific creatures that live below the light zone.

title: Our Mothers' Names: Love in Many Languages
author: Uma Menon
orbital_description: Confirmed April 22, 2025. Opens the linguistics of maternal naming conventions across languages — Amma, Ima, Māmā, Máthair — and the concept that language is a container for culture, so that what you call your mother tells the story of who you are.

title: Papá's Magical Water-Jug Clock
author: Jesús Trejo
orbital_description: The 2024 Belpré Honor book opens the history of water clocks as one of the first timekeeping technologies, the physics of water flow, and the economics of a family that makes its own tools. The clock is real and buildable; the science is accurate.

title: Phoenix
author: Kimberly Brubaker Bradley
orbital_description: Pub March 3, 2026. Kimberly Brubaker Bradley (Jefferson's Sons, Fighting Words, Newbery Honor) opens equine behavior and communication science, the rural geography and economics of horse country, and the SEL architecture of a trust relationship built between a child and an animal that has learned not to trust humans.

title: Planting the Wild Garden
author: Kathryn O. Galbraith
orbital_description: Kathryn Galbraith follows seeds as they travel by wind, water, animal fur, bird droppings, and human shoes. Wendy Anderson Halperin's delicate pencil-and-watercolor illustrations carry botanical accuracy (seed morphology, dispersal mechanisms, germination conditions) while the text carries the poetry of unintentional planting. The child absorbs plant biology, seed engineering, ecosystem interdependence, and the idea that wildflowers are the product of systems, not accidents.

title: Pony
author: R.J. Palacio
orbital_description: The book opens 1860s Ohio and frontier geography, the natural history of the American frontier including landscapes and wildlife, and the ethics of frontier justice. Palacio layers supernatural elements over historically accurate terrain.
heads_up: Violence depicted in a frontier context.

title: Poppy
author: Avi
orbital_description: The owl's actual hunting behaviors including silent flight and head rotation are accurate; the new corn field represents real agricultural land use; the porcupine quill as weapon is real physics. The heroism is built entirely on biology.

title: Press Here
author: Herve Tullet
orbital_description: Tullet instructs the child to press, shake, tilt, and blow on the pages. Input produces output. The child IS the processor.

title: Radiant
author: Vaunda Micheaux Nelson
orbital_description: ALSC 2026 Notable. Vaunda Micheaux Nelson (No Crystal Stair, Coretta Scott King Author Honor) opens the civil rights era in the North through the specific geography of an integrated but hostile school in 1963 Pennsylvania, the economics of domestic work, and the social-emotional experience of being the only Black child in a white classroom at the moment civil rights law was being made.

title: Rain!
author: Linda Ashman
orbital_description: A grumpy man and a joyful boy experience the same rainstorm from opposite emotional poles. Christian Robinson's collage illustrations carry the meteorology (clouds forming, puddles collecting) while the text carries the emotional science: how the same event lands differently depending on who you are. The book resolves with connection, not correction. Neither reaction is wrong.

title: Ranger's Apprentice: The Ruins of Gorlan
author: John Flanagan
orbital_description: Opens the history of medieval intelligence operations, archery as a physics problem (trajectory, draw weight, wind compensation), wilderness tracking as a science of observation and inference, and the feudal social structure through the ward system that defines Will's status.

title: Remarkably Ruby
author: Terri Libenson
orbital_description: The graphic novel opens dual narrative perspective as a formal technique, the social dynamics of the transition from elementary to middle school, anxiety as a hidden experience invisible from the outside, and theater as a space for identity exploration. The hybrid text-and-comics format models two reading modes simultaneously.

title: Revolutionary Mary: The True Story of One Woman, the Declaration of Independence, and America's Fight for Freedom
author: Karen Blumenthal and Jen McCartney
orbital_description: The multiple starred-review picture book biography opens the history of the printing press as a tool of revolution, the specific history of American newspapers during the Revolutionary War, the biography of Mary Katharine Goddard as publisher and postmaster, and the deliberate erasure of women's contributions from the official historical record.

title: Rosie Revere, Engineer
author: Andrea Beaty
orbital_description: Engineering meets WWII history meets growth mindset. The design process is embedded in the plot.

title: Rumpelstiltskin
author: Mac Barnett
orbital_description: Kirkus Spring 2026 Preview top pick, starred review. Opens the European folk tale tradition of bargain stories, the history of spinning and weaving as women's economic labor, the geography of medieval German culture embedded in the original tale, and the craft of fairy tale retelling as literary art. Ellis's art earned the comparison to medieval manuscript illumination.

title: Sakina and the Uninvited Guests
author: Zahra Marwan
orbital_description: Confirmed April 29, 2025. Zahra Marwan opens the concept of art as a time machine — how paintings and sculptures contain the lives of people who made and used them — the history embedded in museum collections, and the social-emotional concept of finding yourself reflected in historical art.

title: Sea in My Cells
author: Laura Alary
orbital_description: Confirmed May 6, 2025. Opens the biology of water in living cells including the water content of blood, tears, and cytoplasm, the evolutionary history of life emerging from the ocean, and the water cycle as the loop that connects the sea to every living body. After this book, children understand why they are made of water.

title: Seven Skies All at Once
author: Ted Kooser
orbital_description: Confirmed July 8, 2025. Ted Kooser (former U.S. Poet Laureate) opens the meteorology of a storm system through the sensory experience of watching a sky change — the specific color shifts of cumulonimbus clouds, the stillness before lightning, the smell of rain — using poetry as the precise instrument for weather observation.

title: Stellaluna
author: Janell Cannon
orbital_description: Stellaluna is secretly a bat biology textbook: echolocation, nocturnal behavior, fruit-eating, and bat anatomy appear throughout. Alongside the science, the book explores the cost of belonging and the relief of being exactly who you are.

title: Steve Jobs: The Man Who Thought Different
author: Karen Blumenthal
orbital_description: The book opens Silicon Valley geography and history, the design philosophy behind Apple products, the economics of the personal computer revolution, and the question of whether visionary leadership and decent behavior are compatible.

title: Stone Soup
author: Jon J Muth
orbital_description: Jon J Muth relocates the European folk tale to China and replaces soldiers with Zen monks. The watercolor style carries Chinese landscape painting traditions while the story carries behavioral economics: how the monks engineer generosity by modeling it. Each villager contributes one ingredient, and the child absorbs nutrition, community dynamics, the psychology of scarcity versus abundance, and the structure of cumulative narratives. The lesson is not about soup. It is about how trust builds when someone goes first.

title: Summer at Squee
author: Andrea Wang
orbital_description: Charlotte Huck Honor 2025. Andrea Wang (Magic Ramen, ALSC Notable) opens the social-emotional experience of a Chinese American girl navigating identity in a space where she doesn't quite fit any category, and the geography of summer camp as a container for rapid self-discovery. NOTE: May be 2024 pub — verify.

title: Sundust
author: Zeke Peña
orbital_description: The 2026 Caldecott Honor Book opens Southwestern desert ecology through the role of solar energy in a desert ecosystem, the geography of the American Southwest, and the visual physics of light across different times of day. Peña's illustration style draws from his Chicano graphic arts tradition to make the science radiant.

title: Tanning the Hide
author: Karina Iceberg
orbital_description: PW starred (January 2026 PW new and noteworthy). Debut by Aleut-Alutiiq author Karina Iceberg. Opens the chemistry and biology of hide tanning as a traditional preservation technique, the specific geography and culture of Aleut communities, the concept of community knowledge as the accumulated science of generations, and the importance of beginning with gratitude.

title: The Bear Out There
author: Jess Hannigan
orbital_description: The ALSC 2026 Notable Book uses a Goldilocks inversion: a narrator whose total certainty is visually contradicted on every spread. The book teaches perspective-taking, the cost of overconfidence, and visual literacy. The reader knows more than the narrator from the opening page.

title: The Beetle Book
author: Steve Jenkins
orbital_description: Steve Jenkins uses his signature cut-paper collage to present beetles at actual size, from the titan beetle (6.5 inches) to nearly invisible species. Each spread covers a different adaptation: bioluminescence, chemical defense, camouflage, horn combat, dung rolling. The child absorbs entomology, evolutionary adaptation, comparative anatomy, and global biogeography (beetles from six continents). Jenkins' art technique itself teaches scale, proportion, and the relationship between illustration and scientific communication.

title: The Book With No Pictures
author: B.J. Novak
orbital_description: The book teaches that language creates images; that reading aloud is performative; that words have power over the speaker. Children discover they can make an adult say almost anything if it is written in a book.

title: The Brilliant Deep: Rebuilding the World's Coral Reefs
author: Kate Messner
orbital_description: Opens the marine biology of coral through the specific biology of coral polyps (animals, not plants), the chemistry of ocean acidification and its effect on calcium carbonate shell-building, the conservation science of coral reef restoration including the fragment cultivation technique Nedimyer developed, and the geography of the Florida Keys as a fragile marine ecosystem.

title: The City of Ember
author: Jeanne DuPrau
orbital_description: Opens the physics of electrical systems through Ember's failing generators, the concept of a closed social system running out of resources, the engineering challenge of a self-sustaining underground environment, and the philosophy of what a society does when it discovers it is not everything it believed it was.

title: The Clock
author: Pam Fong
orbital_description: ALSC 2026 Notable. Opens the history of the Gare d'Orsay as a train station converted to one of the world's great art museums, the craft of clock restoration and horological history, the geography of Paris's cultural institutions, and the concept of preservation as a form of cultural memory.

title: The Dark Lord of Derkholm
author: Diana Wynne Jones
orbital_description: Carnegie Medal. Opens the economics of cultural tourism through the satirical lens of a fantasy world treated as an amusement park, the structure of epic fantasy as a genre through its systematic parody, the ecology of a fantasy world as a real functioning ecosystem, and the concept of what happens when a culture is commodified for outsiders' entertainment.

title: The Dot
author: Peter H. Reynolds
orbital_description: Vashti cannot draw. Her teacher says: make a mark and see where it takes you. She jabs a dot. The teacher frames it. What follows is an arc through color theory, artistic confidence, mentorship dynamics, and the moment a child discovers that creation does not require permission or perfection. Reynolds' watercolors carry the visual art curriculum while the story carries the emotional one. The last page passes the torch to a younger child.

title: The Fabulous Fannie Farmer: The Woman Who Changed the Way America Cooks
author: Emma Bland Smith
orbital_description: The 2025 Best STEM Book winner opens the chemistry of cooking through standardized measurement, the history of domestic science as a legitimate discipline, Boston geography and the cooking school tradition, and the biography of a woman who turned cooking into a science by insisting on precision. The recipes she standardized are in the back.

title: The Good Egg
author: Jory John
orbital_description: Jory John personifies a good egg who does everything right: cleans up, helps everyone, holds it together while the other eggs are rotten. He cracks from the effort. Pete Oswald's illustrations carry the physical metaphor (the crack, the bandage, the slow repair) while the text carries the psychology of perfectionism, people-pleasing, and burnout. The resolution is not selfishness. It is boundaries. The child absorbs emotional vocabulary for burnout, the difference between helping and overextending, and the biology of eggs as a surprisingly effective metaphor for structural integrity under stress.

title: The Great Wall of Lucy Wu
author: Wendy Wan-Long Shang
orbital_description: Chinese-American identity through a girl who wants to be normal and a grandmother who refuses to let her forget.

title: The Hello Goodbye Window
author: Norton Juster
orbital_description: The book is a love letter to the grandparent-grandchild relationship and to finding magic in the ordinary: a window, a garden, a hug. It teaches children to notice what they already have.

title: The Hive Detectives: Chronicle of a Honey Bee Catastrophe
author: Loree Griffin Burns
orbital_description: Sibert Honor 2011. Opens the biology of honeybees including the social organization of the hive through caste roles (queen, workers, drones), the ecology of pollination as the mechanism connecting bees to the entire food system, the scientific investigation process through the multiple research teams pursuing different hypotheses for Colony Collapse Disorder, and the concept of a sentinel species as an indicator of ecosystem health.

title: The Ink Witch
author: Steph Cherrywell
orbital_description: PW starred + Kirkus starred (2025). Opens the concept of art-making as a form of magic through the visual metaphor of sentient ink, the history of illustration as craft, and the social-emotional arc of a young person discovering that their creative power is greater and stranger than they were taught. The graphic novel format makes the ink's behavior visible in ways prose cannot.

title: The Last Stand
author: Antwan Eady
orbital_description: Charlotte Huck Award Winner 2025. Antwan Eady (Nigel and the Moon) opens the economic history of Black-owned businesses in America through the specific geography of a neighborhood grocery store, the concept of community commerce as cultural preservation, and the social-emotional weight of a business that is also a community institution. NOTE: May be 2024 pub — verify.

title: The Listening Walk
author: Paul Showers
orbital_description: A science book about sound waves disguised as a walk around the block.

title: The Lumbering Giants of Windy Pines
author: Mo Netz
orbital_description: The Kirkus Best of 2024 novel opens forest ecology through the specific biology of old-growth woodland, disability and accessibility as lived experience rather than narrative obstacle, and the mystery structure of a community secret kept for decades. The protagonist's wheelchair is a fact, not a plot device.

title: The Map Trap
author: Andrew Clements
orbital_description: Cartography as both skill and ethical dilemma.

title: The Marvellers
author: Dhonielle Clayton
orbital_description: The book opens the history of conjure as a magical tradition rooted in real African American folk practice, the social dynamics of being first in an institution that was not built for you, and the mystery structure of a disappearance that only Ella can solve. The school's global architecture borrows from real world traditions.

title: The Mysterious Benedict Society
author: Trenton Lee Stewart
orbital_description: Opens Morse code as a communication technology, the psychology of persuasion and propaganda through the antagonist's methods, puzzle-solving as a collaborative skill, and the dynamics of four children with wildly different abilities learning to trust each other. Every puzzle is solvable by the reader alongside the characters.

title: The Name Jar
author: Yangsook Choi
orbital_description: Unhei moves from Korea to America and faces the universal immigrant dilemma: assimilate or hold. Her classmates fill a jar with name suggestions. Yangsook Choi draws both Korean and American classroom cultures with equal respect, and the child absorbs Korean naming traditions, the linguistics of transliteration, the social dynamics of a new school, and the weight of a name as cultural inheritance. Unhei's decision at the end is not a compromise. It is a claim.

title: The Nine Moons of Han Yu and Luli
author: Karina Yan Glaser
orbital_description: The 2026 Newbery Honor and Belpré Honor Book opens Chinese mythology and its astronomical roots, the actual science of lunar cycles and the Chinese lunar calendar, Chinese American immigrant family experience, and sibling dynamics as a parallel to the mythological sister bond.

title: The One and Only Ivan
author: Katherine Applegate
orbital_description: Based on the real Ivan. Applegate writes in Ivan's voice: short, spare, observational. Newbery Medal.
heads_up: Animal captivity. An elephant character dies.

title: The One and Only Ruby
author: Katherine Applegate
orbital_description: The third One and Only novel opens elephant biology including memory, communication, and grief, the ecology and operations of an animal sanctuary, and the psychology of a young animal navigating the social world of her species after early trauma. The science of elephant cognition is woven into Ruby's daily choices.

title: The Poisoned King
author: Katherine Rundell
orbital_description: The ALSC 2026 Notable Book continues the Impossible Creatures series, a fantasy built on the premise that mythological creatures are real and governed by ecological systems. The dying dragons open conservation biology through a fantasy lens, island biogeography through the Archipelago world-building, and the ethics of intervention in natural systems.

title: The Pout-Pout Fish
author: Deborah Diesen
orbital_description: The book introduces ocean animals through their encounters with the fish while modeling fixed versus growth mindset. The fish's transformation is a lesson in how identity is not fixed at birth.

title: The Recess Queen
author: Alexis O'Neill
orbital_description: The book models bystander behavior, the social architecture of bullying, and the disarming power of unafraid friendliness. Katie Sue changes Mean Jean not through confrontation but through genuine invitation, which is what the research actually supports.

title: The Secret Life of a Sea Turtle
author: Maddalena Bearzi
orbital_description: Kirkus starred 'Mesmerizing and insightful.' By the co-founder of the Ocean Conservation Society, the book opens sea turtle biology including magnetic navigation, deep diving physiology, and nesting behavior, the oceanography of the routes sea turtles follow, and the conservation crisis facing all seven species.

title: The Shrew Detective: The Case of the Pilfered Pearls
author: Margi Preus
orbital_description: Lit Hub Most Anticipated 2026. Margi Preus (Shadow on the Mountain, Heart of a Samurai) opens the biology of shrews including their remarkable olfactory sense and metabolism, the geography and social history of the Victorian era when the story is set, and the detective genre structure as a framework for teaching observational reasoning. Pub May 19, 2026.

title: The Storm Runner
author: Jennifer Cervantes
orbital_description: Rick Riordan Presents. Opens Maya mythology through the Popol Vuh and specific Maya pantheon, the geography of Mesoamerica, the science of volcanoes, and the Mexican American diaspora experience. Cervantes draws from authentic Maya sources.

title: The Tenth Mistake of Hank Hooperman
author: Gennifer Choldenko
orbital_description: From the author of Al Capone Does My Shirts comes a middle grade novel about a boy whose history of spectacular mistakes forces him to reckon with the pattern. The book opens the psychology of repeated errors and the community that forms around a known quantity, with Choldenko's signature warmth and period-accurate setting detail.

title: The Truth about Dragons
author: Julie Leung
orbital_description: The 2024 Caldecott Honor book opens comparative mythology through the lens of the world's most globally beloved creature: the dragon. Leung and Cha place Eastern and Western dragon traditions side by side with visual precision, teaching children that truth changes depending on where you stand. After this one, children start asking which version of any story they've been told.

title: The Ugly Five
author: Julia Donaldson
orbital_description: African savanna ecology taught through a celebration of ugly. Each unlovely feature is actually an adaptation.

title: The Very Quiet Cricket
author: Eric Carle
orbital_description: Every animal the cricket meets communicates differently: bees buzz, locusts chirp, praying mantises rustle. The book quietly introduces animal communication science while building emotional vocabulary around patience and persistence.

title: The Way I Feel
author: Janan Cain
orbital_description: The book gives children names for the full spectrum of emotion including angry, sad, frightened, proud, happy, jealous, silly, and frustrated. Each is illustrated with physical correlates, teaching body-awareness alongside emotional vocabulary.

title: The Wild Robot Protects
author: Peter Brown
orbital_description: The third Wild Robot book opens climate science through the specific ecological consequences Roz's island faces, the engineering limits of a machine trying to solve an environmental problem, and the question of whether technology or nature holds the answer to ecological crisis. The seasonal structure maps a full ecological cycle.

title: The Winter of the Dollhouse
author: Laura Amy Schlitz
orbital_description: ALSC 2026 Notable. Laura Amy Schlitz (Good Masters! Sweet Ladies!, Newbery Medal) opens the history of antique dollhouses as social artifacts reflecting the lives of the households they miniaturize, the social-emotional architecture of an intergenerational friendship between a child and an elderly woman, and the concept of a doll as a carrier of historical memory.

title: The World Is Waiting for You
author: Barbara Kerley
orbital_description: Barbara Kerley pairs childhood photos of famous explorers, scientists, and artists with photographs of their adult achievements: Jane Goodall as a girl with a stuffed chimp, then with real chimps; a young surfer who became an oceanographer; a kid building model planes who became a pilot. National Geographic photography carries the geographic and scientific scope while the structure carries the biographical argument that childhood interests, pursued with seriousness, become adult expertise. The child absorbs career pathways, global geography, and the connection between play and profession.

title: This Is Not My Hat
author: Jon Klassen
orbital_description: The book teaches visual literacy, ocean habitat, and the consequences of theft through the most perfectly timed reveal in picture book comedy. The big fish's eyes tell the real story before the words do.

title: Those Shoes
author: Maribeth Boelts
orbital_description: Consumer economics at child scale. Wants-versus-needs embedded in the plot.

title: Tiny But Mighty
author: Hannah Shaw
orbital_description: Kitten rescue as a science education platform. Applied science with real stakes.
heads_up: Some kittens do not survive.

title: Tiny, Perfect Things
author: M.H. Clark
orbital_description: M.H. Clark builds the entire book around the practice of noticing: a spiderweb with dew, a ladybug on a leaf, a crack in the sidewalk with a flower growing through it. Madeline Kloepper's illustrations carry botanical and entomological detail at the micro-scale while the text carries the relationship between a grandparent who teaches attention and a child who learns it. The child absorbs observational science, micro-ecology, and the discipline of looking closely, which is the foundation of every scientific method.

title: To Market, To Market
author: Anushka Ravishankar
orbital_description: Anushka Ravishankar takes the old nursery rhyme and detonates it into an Indian marketplace. The woman buys a fat red hen, then a fat red cow, then escalating animals until the house is a zoo and the counting is cumulative mathematics under pressure. Emanuele Scanziani's illustrations carry the visual density of an Indian bazaar: spices, textiles, produce, livestock, architecture. The child absorbs counting, cumulative addition, Indian market culture, animal classification, and the narrative principle that comedy comes from escalation.

title: To See an Owl
author: Matthew Cordell
orbital_description: SLJ Best Picture Book 2025. Matthew Cordell (Wolf in the Snow, Caldecott Medal) opens owl biology including nocturnal behavior, camouflage, and silent flight, the ecology of night, and the scientific practice of patient observation. The social-emotional layer is about sustained attention as a form of love for the natural world.

title: Too Much: An Overwhelming Day
author: Jolene Gutierrez
orbital_description: The book opens sensory processing disorder through a child's lived experience, the neuroscience of sensory overwhelm, and the specific comfort of deep-pressure touch. Chang's evocative illustrations make sensory input visible, helping all children understand why some experiences feel unbearable.

title: Tracking Trash: Flotsam, Jetsam, and the Science of Ocean Motion
author: Loree Griffin Burns
orbital_description: Opens the oceanography of gyres and thermohaline circulation through the tracking of specific floating debris items, the scientific method through Curtis Ebbesmeyer's use of lost cargo as unplanned scientific experiments, the geography of Pacific Ocean current systems, and the ecological concept of ocean plastic as a persistent environmental tracer.

title: Tristan Strong Punches a Hole in the Sky
author: Kwame Mbalia
orbital_description: Rick Riordan Presents. Opens West African mythology through the Anansi stories and Akan spiritual tradition, the history of African American folk heroes as figures of resistance, and the social-emotional architecture of grief worked through a mythological adventure.

title: Tuck Me In! A Science Bedtime Story
author: Nathan W. Pyle
orbital_description: NPR Best 2025 opens sleep science including circadian rhythm, the role of sleep in memory consolidation, cellular repair during sleep, and the biology of night. The bedtime ritual format makes the science feel like a lullaby; the content is accurate and age-calibrated. Pyle's distinctive visual style bridges science explanation and emotional warmth.

title: Unflappable
author: Matthew Ward
orbital_description: The book opens animal biology through flightless bird anatomy, engineering design cycles through the birds' increasingly inventive machines, and the psychology of persistence through repeated creative failure. Each machine is drawn with the specificity of a real engineering diagram.

title: Wemberly Worried
author: Kevin Henkes
orbital_description: The book normalizes anxiety without dismissing it, models social problem-solving, and shows the relief of shared experience. Wemberly's worry list is a real anxiety inventory parents can use to open conversations.

title: What Do You Do with a Chance
author: Kobi Yamada
orbital_description: The book teaches opportunity cost through the felt experience of a missed chance. The eventual taking of a chance and its reward is not simple success but a return to what was always possible.

title: What Do You Do With an Idea?
author: Kobi Yamada
orbital_description: Companion to What Do You Do With a Problem. The world starts in sepia and the idea is the only color.

title: Will's Race for Home
author: Jewell Parker Rhodes
orbital_description: The 2026 Caldecott Honor and Coretta Scott King Author Award winner opens the Reconstruction-era history of Black jockeys who dominated American horse racing before Jim Crow laws pushed them out, the geography of the Kentucky horse country, and the specific courage of a child navigating a world changing rapidly around him.

title: Wombats Are Pretty Weird: A (Not So) Serious Guide
author: Abi Cushman
orbital_description: The book opens wombat anatomy, marsupial biology, Australian ecology, and the science of cubic feces through a running fictional dialogue between the wombat and the author that models scientific skepticism and fact-checking. Every strange wombat fact is real and sourced.

title: Women in Science: 50 Fearless Pioneers Who Changed the World
author: Rachel Ignotofsky
orbital_description: Opens the history of science across multiple disciplines through biographies of women whose contributions were often credited to others, the geography of scientific history across multiple countries, and the graphic design concept of using illustration to make dense biographical information emotionally accessible.

title: Xolo: How One Good Dog Saved Humankind
author: Donna Barba Higuera
orbital_description: ALSC 2026 Notable, Middle category. Opens Aztec cosmology through the creation myth of Quetzalcoatl and Xolotl, the natural history and anthropology of the xoloitzcuintli as a breed with 3,000 years of recorded history in Mesoamerica, and the geography of pre-Columbian Mexico.
